subject: LumenCare: commitments on model training and ownership of prompts/responses
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@lumencare.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: LumenCare Legal <legal@lumencare.io>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify commitments re: model training and prompt/response ownership

Hi Soojin / Karthik,

Following up from our security call earlier — legal has asked for a written summary of Redwood's position and what you can commit to contractually. Specifically LumenCare wants to understand:

- Whether Redwood will agree to a contractual prohibition on using customer prompts/responses for model improvement (i.e., a binding "training exclusion").
- If you cannot commit for the hosted product, what technical or contractual mitigations exist (e.g., per-tenant opt-out, retention windows, redaction).
- How Redwood treats ownership of prompts/responses and whether delivery artifacts (generated text, embeddings) are considered customer property or subject to Redwood reuse.
- A list of subprocessors that would see PPAs/inference logs and any SOC2/attestation you can provide.

Can you provide a short written position and the evidence we can share with procurement (sample audit log fields, subprocessor CSV, DPA section references)? Procurement also asked for an export package example showing what we'd receive if LumenCare exercised a data export.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we have a Dec 8 legal milestone for contract signature.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Keller
Sr. Counsel, LumenCare
anna.keller@lumencare.io

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@lumencare.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify commitments re: model training and prompt/response ownership

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Below is our position and what we can contractually offer. Attaching the DPA excerpt (section 3.2) and our current subprocessor inventory for your review.

1) Training exclusion
- Hosted (standard Redwood API): By default, customer prompts and responses may be used to improve service quality (anonymized telemetry and aggregate model tuning).
- Contracted training exclusion: We can add a contractual clause that explicitly prohibits Redwood from using LumenCare input/output pairs for model training or model improvement activities. This clause will be limited to the scope of inference inputs/outputs (not metadata required for operations) and will be time-bound to the contract term.
- Implementation & evidence: For customers who take a training exclusion we provide: a subprocessor attestation, a monthly export of inference-log metadata (fields noted below), and an annual independent attestation of adherence for Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted, we can offer the clause plus operational attestations; for Dedicated and Private we can additionally implement configuration flags that prevent data from entering improvement pipelines.

2) Technical mitigations (hosted + dedicated)
- Per-tenant opt-out: On Dedicated/Private we can toggle an opt-out so the inference pipeline drops customer traffic from analytics/model-improvement stores. For Hosted, opt-out is available under enterprise contract where we route traffic through an exclusion path and provide attestations.
- Retention windows: We can contractually limit retention of raw inference logs to a defined window (e.g., 30/90/180 days) and only retain aggregate telemetry longer for platform health.
- Redaction & tokenization: Options exist to apply customer-provided PII redaction rules before logs are stored; we can also integrate with your KMS to avoid storing plaintext secrets.

3) Ownership of prompts and responses
- Delivered outputs (the text, embeddings, reranks returned to your API calls) are considered customer data and we will not claim ownership. You may use them as you see fit.
- Derivative rights: Redwood will not assert rights to derivative works you build from prompts/responses. The training exclusion ensures we do not add those artifacts into model training corpora.

4) Subprocessors & evidence
- See attached subprocessor CSV. Subprocessors who handle inference logs include our cloud infra partner(s) and monitoring vendors — we list those and their purpose.
- We can provide SOC2 coverage statements for primary subprocessors and an evidence package (sample audit log export format, schema).

5) Export package example
- We will produce an export ZIP containing: raw inference log CSV (timestamp, request_id, model, input_hash, output_text, latency_ms), retention annotations, and a minimal redaction map if applicable. For security, export bundles are delivered via an authenticated signed link and can be routed to your S3 if preferred.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-section-3.2.pdf (DPA excerpt), subprocessor-inventory-2026-11.csv (current list).

I'll loop in Karthik for a short technical note on caches/kv and Marissa on contractual language. Happy to draft proposed contract text for the training exclusion and retention table.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@lumencare.io>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify commitments re: model training and prompt/response ownership

Anna — quick technical addendum to clarify where customer content touches system components and what we can toggle:

- Inference path: Incoming requests are processed by the serving runtime. Short-term KV cache (per-request) is in-memory and not persisted. Persistent inference logs are written to an encrypted log store when retention rules allow.
- Model improvement pipeline: A separate analytics pipeline consumes a sanitized stream from the log store. For customers with a contractual training exclusion we switch that stream off for your tenant (or route it to a zero-write sink).
- KV/Prefix caching: Prefix caches used to speed repeated calls are ephemeral by default. We can disable cross-tenant caches for your account and ensure caches are zeroed on session termination for Dedicated/Private.
- Encryption & key management: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can integrate with your key provider under enterprise agreements to minimize plaintext exposure.

If you want, I can produce a one-page diagram showing these flows and toggles for the contract annex.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@lumencare.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-05T15:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify commitments re: model training and prompt/response ownership

Thanks — this is helpful. Legal has a few follow ups before we can sign the training-exclusion addendum:

- Please provide a sample export bundle (anonymized) so we can validate column names and hash strategies.
- Procurement would like the subprocessor SOC2 statements (or equivalent letters) for the infra vendors that see inference logs.
- Our team wants the draft redline language for the training exclusion + the retention table (30/90/180 options) — we will mark the draft with in-line comments.

I've attached our redline request doc (LumenCare-DPA-redline-requests.docx). Can you send the sample export and the proposed contract text by EOD Dec 8? Our procurement deadline is firm.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Anna
Anna Keller
Sr. Counsel, LumenCare
